{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us. Of the eighteen playbook rules reviewed, fourteen are compliant with no redline required, including all of the critical protections other than liability: Vendor's indemnity (§ 20) exceeds our preferred position and is uncapped as an Excluded Claim, ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data sits with us (§ 14), the licence grant covers Affiliates and contractors and includes a perpetual paid-up licence (§ 13), assignment and change-of-control controls run our way (§ 24), and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicit obligation binding us. Governing law and venue are New York, as preferred (§ 28).

Two issues are material and both fall into walk-away territory:

- **Limitation of liability cap (§ 21).** The architecture is good — mutual cap, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and broad Excluded Claims — but "Fees" is defined (§§ 1.5/1.6) as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The cap is therefore roughly USD 12,000 regardless of ongoing spend, which is far below six months' fees and effectively illusory.
- **Liquidated damages for late payment (§ 7.7).** Customer owes Vendor 15% of annual Fees per week an invoice is late, triggered by a ten-day delay. Compounding, this exceeds the entire annual contract value in about seven weeks. Both our preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees) fail.

Two further findings carry a **needs_review** status where automated verification did not pass; on the substance recorded in the findings both appear compliant, and neither requires a commercial concession from Vendor. They are listed below so the team can confirm before signature.

---

## 2. Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 | Cap measured on the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form only; illusory, walk-away. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 | Exceeds preferred position; no Customer-modification/combination exclusions; uncapped as an Excluded Claim under § 21.3. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 | We own Customer Data and Deliverables; no joint ownership; no model-training or aggregate-data grab (§ 15.1). |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 (7.7) | 15% of annual Fees per week late; walk-away territory. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 | Free Customer assignment to Affiliate/successor; Vendor consent-gated and never to a competitor. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 | § 12.3 affirmatively disclaims exclusivity; § 12.4 restraint binds Vendor. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 | Affiliates/contractors covered; perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence; revocation only for uncured material breach. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12 | No field-of-use or business restraint on us; § 13.4 limits are ordinary use restrictions. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 (9.4) | 30 days' notice (§ 29.4), accrued Fees only, prepaid Fees refunded; no Vendor convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 | Annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment, no system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 | New York law; exclusive New York County courts; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 7 (7.6) | Parity runs in our favour; not flagged. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 (2.1) | No minimum quantity; declining further orders is not a breach; audit "shortfall" is a true-up only. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review** (verification not passed) | § 12 | No covenant binds Customer; § 12.3 preserves our hiring freedom. Duration/carve-out checks probe a covenant that does not exist. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8 | 12-month renewals, 30 days' opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension, uplift capped at lesser of CPI/3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 | Six months' assistance at Order Form rates; 30-day return in machine-readable form; no withholding for fee disputes. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, WC as required; term plus one year. Cancellation notice qualified by insurer availability (noted only). |
| Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review** (verification not passed) | § 19 | Meets preferred position on substance; 90-day Deliverable warranty and term-long Hosted Services conformance. Period written in words only, no numeral. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These two items are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should not be conceded:

1. **§ 21 — illusory liability cap.** A cap measured on a single USD 12,000 implementation charge is not a meaningful allocation of risk. *Proposed redline:* keep the existing sentence structure and mutual carve-out architecture, but measure the cap by all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor (our preferred position). We have deliberately left the "Fees" definition in §§ 1.5/1.6 untouched so as not to disturb the payment provisions.
2. **§ 7.7 — liquidated damages for late payment.** *Proposed redline:* delete the liquidated damages mechanic and substitute simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as Vendor's sole remedy for late payment.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the two redlines** on § 21 (cap quantum and USD 1,000,000 floor) and § 7.7 (delete liquidated damages; interest on undisputed overdue amounts only). These are the only substantive asks arising from this review.
2. **Clear the two needs_review items internally** before circulating: confirm (a) that no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binding Customer appears anywhere in the document, the deterministic duration and carve-out checks having probed for terms inside a covenant that does not exist; and (b) the § 19.2 warranty period, where the substance is at least 90 days but the drafting spells out "ninety days" without a numeral. A non-substantive clarification inserting "(90)" is attached and can be dropped if Vendor prefers the words-only form.
3. **Accept as drafted** the fourteen compliant provisions; no comments should be raised on them, including the Vendor-granted pricing parity in § 7.6 and the Vendor-side competitive restraint in § 12.4, both of which benefit us.
4. **Note for the file, not for negotiation:** the qualification of Vendor's cancellation-notice undertaking in § 18.2 by "to the extent available from its insurer"."}
